divergence.reason: TypeScript 7's checker returns the reduced `keyof Params` union with its literal members in sorted-key order (callback, indirectUnion, inlineNumberUnion, …), while the pinned TypeScript 6 oracle preserves the operand's property declaration order (inlineStringUnion, inlineNumberUnion, referencedStringUnion, …). The resolver's canonicalizer is order-preserving for both compilers — a minimal probe (`keyof { zebra; mango; alpha }`) reproduces the sorted order from the checker alone — so the reordering happens inside TypeScript 7's union construction, not in extraction policy. All 7 leaf differences are confined to the `resolvedType` member values of the one preserved operator; every other shape matches the upstream oracle, including the compacted named-object operand and the `resolutionKind`.
